svg.text: One device on SIG at a time. Grounds are joined once, at the board.
Board connectors (JST-SH 1.0 mm; the board has no 2.54 mm headers)
GP1 AUX KISS telemetry, servo B
GP0 SIG ESC or servo signal
VBUS USB 5 V, feeds no servo or ESC
GP7 shared I2C bus: do not use
GP6 shared I2C bus: do not use
GP0 SIG ESC or servo signal
GP1 AUX KISS telemetry, servo B
GP28 EN servo supply enable, option
GP29 EN servo supply enable, option
GP7 shared I2C bus: do not use
GP6 shared I2C bus: do not use
USB-C: power and the USB serial port.
LiPo cell: optional, charged by the board.
SIG and AUX are set under
pins of a board with blank flash.
SIG, AUX: GP0, GP1, fault tolerant,
not fault tolerant: an output only.
A ESC: bidirectional DShot on SIG, KISS telemetry on AUX
Cut or depin the ESC lead's middle wire, the BEC +5 V output: it goes to no pin.
Power the ESC from its own battery, never from the board's 5 V. Unplug any servo before DShot runs.
B Servo, supply switched by hand: servo tester, KST, Hitec D series
servo supply: 5 V for KST and Hitec;
tester 4.8 V to 6.0 V, 8.4 V for HV
The servo's middle wire goes to its supply, never to a connector pin. Power the board before the servo supply,
and switch the servo supply off first. KST answers only just after power-up: switch the supply on when the screen
searches. Power a Hitec D series servo before tapping D SERIES.
C Servo on the switched supply: KST, Hitec D series and classic (SETTINGS > SERVO SUPPLY GP28)
DC-DC: > 1 A; buck, or output disconnect;
e.g. Pololu S13V30F5, 2.8 V to 22 V in
EN on GP28 (J4 pin 11) or GP29 (J4 pin 12), with SERVO SUPPLY at that pin. SIG, EN and GND share one J4 pigtail;
J5 stays free. The pull-down sits at the converter: 10 kΩ for the Pololu S13V30F5, whose EN has a 475 kΩ
pull-up; 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ for an EN without one. EN is high only during a KST or Hitec claim. The servo tester
does not switch it: a servo there needs a supply of its own. An ESC on this lead gets VOUT on its BEC wire.
